description: Capability for the popover window. Kept minimal — the popover is render-only and never spawns processes or reads the filesystem directly; it talks to Rust exclusively through get_state()/refresh_now/hide_popover/state-changed. T8/F3 (sec review, tightened again for T9 D2): scoped to exactly the IPC surface src/ actually calls, not the broad core:default bundle — core:event:allow-listen for the state-changed subscription AND the window focus/blur events onFocusChanged listens to (both delivered over the SAME generic event-listen permission, no separate core:window:* grant needed), plus the three app commands (auto-generated by build.rs's AppManifest, see permissions/autogenerated/). allow-hide-popover is the one addition for D2 (Esc / click-outside dismiss) — still just a hide, not a general window-control grant: no show/focus/move/resize/close-window permission exists here, and no fs/shell/http/dialog plugin is linked at all. Opening the popover remains Rust-only (tray click handler / CT_SHOW_POPOVER_ON_LAUNCH test hook); the webview can only ever ask Rust to hide it, never show it.
